p: A visit to York Maze is a proper outdoor day rather than a quick stop, so most families find it easiest to settle in for several hours. Pack a picnic and plenty of water, because racing around the paths in summer sunshine is thirsty work, and the maize gives very little shade.

With younger children, agree a plan before you set off into the maze. Decide who's sticking with who and pick an easy meeting point in case your group gets split up. It's half the fun to try different routes, but tiny explorers can get frustrated if they're tired, so be ready to take a break and come back to it.

A pushchair isn't always the best friend in a field, especially after rain, so a baby carrier or sling can make life much easier for the smallest visitors. Older kids and teens usually love the freedom of charging around on their own, and they'll want to beat the grown-ups to the finish, naturally.

The maze sits near Elvington, a short drive from York, so it pairs nicely with a day or two in the city. York itself is packed with history: walk part of the medieval city walls, gaze up at the Minster, mooch along the Shambles or spend a few hours at the National Railway Museum. Right on the maze's doorstep, the Yorkshire Air Museum at Elvington is another good one if you've got aviation fans in the family.
If your trip lands outside the summer season, the maze won't be open, so plan around the crop rather than the calendar.
